deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page): K(x) = K(x1,x2,...) is a bounded quadratic form in infinitely many variables. It is assumed definite and without point spectrum. It has the spectral representation K(x) = ∫_α^∞ (ψ1(μ)x1 + ψ2(μ)x2 + …)^2 / μ dμ, so its continuous spectrum, in Hilbert's λ-convention where the eigenvalue condition is (x,x) − λK(x) = 0, starts at μ = α. K_n denotes the n-th section of K, i.e. the form in x1..xn with all other variables set to 0. λ_1^(n) is the smallest characteristic value of K_n, so 1/λ_1^(n) is the largest value of K_n on the unit sphere. The λ_1^(n) accumulate at β, the point of the spectrum nearest λ = 0. Hilbert calls it 'point spectrum', though no point spectrum is assumed. The problem is the max/min problem for an infinite quadratic form via the spectral representation, announced on the previous page. Hilbert wants to show that the bottom of the spectrum equals the limit of the section values: α = β.

Step 1 (approach 1/β from below). K_n attains 1/λ_1^(n) at some unit vector (x1..xn). Padding with zeros, K attains the same value at a unit vector. Since λ_1^(n) → β, for suitable choices of x one gets values of K(x) on (x,x) = 1 arbitrarily close to 1/β. Implicitly (my addition): the values 1/λ_1^(n) increase with n, so sup_{(x,x)=1} K(x) ≥ 1/β.

Step 2 (upper bound). With no point spectrum and K definite, the unit form has the completeness representation (x,x) = ∫_α^∞ (ψ1(μ)x1 + …)^2 dμ. Since 1/μ ≤ 1/α on [α,∞), K(x) ≤ (1/α)(x,x), i.e. K(x) ≤ 1/α on the unit sphere. Hence 1/β ≤ 1/α. With α, β > 0 this gives β ≥ α. Hilbert writes 'd.h. α ≧ β', which is a slip.

Step 3 (reverse inequality). α is a point of the continuous spectrum, and the continuous spectrum lies entirely in the spectrum. β is the spectral point nearest 0, so β ≤ α. Together: α = β.

In modern terms: for a bounded positive self-adjoint operator, sup of the Rayleigh quotient equals max of the spectrum (here 1/α in eigenvalue terms). This value is the limit of the largest eigenvalues of the finite sections.

Second part (foundations of geometry, Frege controversy). Frege had produced a nonsense sentence in his 1906 Jahresbericht papers 'Über die Grundlagen der Geometrie'. Hilbert recalls it garbled here, and on the next page as 'Anz bazet mindestens 2 Tekmisek'; Frege's original is, as I recall, 'Jedes Anej bazet wenigstens zwei Ellah'. Frege's aim was to parody Hilbert's implicit definitions. Hilbert's reply:
- The example shows only Frege's ability to form senseless sentences, not anything against his theory.
- His axioms always have the form '… ist zugeordnet …'. The relation 'zugeordnet' is taken as known and fixed prior to all logic, and must be: the mind's capacity to relate things to things has to be presupposed.
- Frege has therefore misunderstood the sense and purpose of the Grundlagen.
- Of course one may say other words instead of 'Punkte', 'Gerade', 'Ebene', 'zwischen', but that is nothing new.
- He had explicitly remarked that 'liegen auf', 'gehen durch', 'enthalten' mean nothing other than 'zugeordnet sein'.

The next page shows this was drafted as a possible footnote, which was never published.
errors: From 1/β ≤ 1/α (α, β > 0) follows β ≥ α, i.e. α ≤ β. Hilbert writes 'd.h. α ≧ β', which is the same inequality as the later 'β ≦ α'. As written the two halves do not combine to α = β; with the slip corrected the argument is sound.

The previous page calls β 'die λ=0 nächstgelegene Stelle des Punktspektrums', although K is assumed to have no point spectrum. 'Spektrum' is meant: β is the limit of the section eigenvalues and, by Step 3, the nearest spectral point.

Implicit assumptions, all standard in Hilbert's 1906 theory: the completeness relation (x,x) = ∫(ψ·x)^2 dμ, which needs definiteness and no point spectrum; α > 0 (boundedness of K); and that the λ_1^(n) converge, which holds since they decrease monotonically.

results.what: For a definite bounded quadratic form with purely continuous spectrum starting at α, the limit β of the smallest section eigenvalues λ_1^(n) equals α. Equivalently, sup K(x) on (x,x) = 1 is 1/α, the extreme spectral point.
results.modern_name: Rayleigh quotient / variational characterization of the top of the spectrum (norm of a positive self-adjoint operator); convergence of finite-section (Ritz) approximations
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert, 4th Mitteilung on integral equations (1906) and Hellinger's dissertation (1907); later von Neumann/Stone in operator language

results.what: Reply to Frege's nonsense-word parody: axioms are statements about a primitive relation 'zugeordnet', fixed before logic; the names of the objects are arbitrary.
results.modern_name: Implicit definition / structuralist (formal-axiomatic) view of axioms; Frege–Hilbert controversy
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (Grundlagen der Geometrie 1899; letters to Frege 1899–1900); Frege's critique 1903/1906

deep.surprise_reason: The spectral argument is a routine special case of Hilbert's own 1906 spectral theory, with a small inequality slip. The Frege passage shows Hilbert drafting a private, never-published reply to Frege's 1906 papers, including an explicit 'vor aller Logik' status for the primitive relation of assignment. That is a mildly interesting unpublished detail for historians, but it fits his known dismissive attitude and his known structuralist view.

checkable.asserts: For positive α, β, 1/β ≤ 1/α implies β ≥ α. Hilbert's 'α ≧ β' at this step is a slip.
The largest eigenvalue of a section is nondecreasing in n (Cauchy interlacing): 3 ≤ 2+sqrt(2). So 1/λ_1^(n) increases and λ_1^(n) decreases to its limit β.
Example: the sections of the tridiagonal (2,1) Toeplitz form have top eigenvalue 2+2cos(π/(n+1)). These approach 4, the supremum of its purely continuous spectrum [0,4], illustrating α = β.

transcription_corrections: Frege's nonsense sentence is misread or garbled. The image reads roughly 'Ellaj baset mindestens 2 Tesknisek', while the next page has 'Anz bazet mindestens 2 Tekmisek'. Frege's original (Jahresbericht DMV 15, 1906) is, as I recall, 'Jedes Anej bazet wenigstens zwei Ellah', which Hilbert misremembers.
'Natürlich[?] kann[?]' should read 'Natürlich kann man statt …'; the reading is clear in the image.
The struck-out word before 'Geistes' is an aborted 'Ge…'/'Gei…', not an unknown word.
The struck-out word in 'Da α doch [-?-] wirklich' is a short crossed-out word (possibly 'als'); it is immaterial.
The form is written as a script/Fraktur 𝔎(x) on this page, consistent with K(x) on the previous page.
'd.h. α ≧ β' is correctly transcribed: it is Hilbert's own slip, not a transcription error.
